subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: What durable sender identity contract should OpenClaw expose for human, main-agent, and subagent messages across Gateway schemas, persisted session history, live events, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The remaining work changes public Gateway/session semantics and UI identity behavior, so automation should not choose permanent fields or compatibility rules without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add structured sender identity
options.body: Introduce an additive sender identity object with kind, stable id, display name, source session/agent, and optional render metadata, then thread it through Gateway and UI surfaces.

options.title: Keep senderLabel-only patches
options.body: Continue fixing visible attribution regressions with string labels while leaving transcript and live-event identity unresolved.

options.title: Defer broad contract
options.body: Keep only narrow regressions open and defer durable multi-agent identity until a wider messaging model design is scheduled.

recommendation.title: Add structured sender identity
recommendation.body: Introduce an additive sender identity object with kind, stable id, display name, source session/agent, and optional render metadata, then thread it through Gateway and UI surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Most connected to the provenance/session-send context history and already involved in the issue discussion.
